Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Planning Commission Members will be participating via

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter. Commission meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:

a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After

public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 867 0370 7621 Passcode: 736259.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 867 0370
7621 Passcode: 736259.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, AUGUST 2, 2021

  An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
  to order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Edler, Carman, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang

  Commissioners Absent:  Scott

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JULY 6, 2021

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked for clarification on a comment made in Item 7A. After a
  brief discussion, it was agreed that if the comment was verbatim, quotations should be
  added.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 5,
  2021, WITH REVISION.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  APPROVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED
  FOR CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READY BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
  to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210244; ADDRESS: 2 BRANDING IRON LANE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: MR. JOSEPH DANGARAN; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210245) to demolish the existing single-
  story home to construct a new single-story residence.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER recused himself since his firm represents some of the people
  involved.

  Associate Planner Thom presented Planning Application No. PA-210244, a request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to demolish the existing one-story home and garage
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, AUGUST 2, 2021
  1
   and construct a new approximately 5,200 sq. ft. single-story home with an approximately 900 sq.
  ft. multiple car garage. Associate Planner Thom stated that in reference to the term “disputed
  easement” as noted in the staff report, she would prefer to describe the issue as an undetermined
  recorded easement. The city has submitted a records request to the Los Angeles County
  Recorder's Office to determine if there are any such recorded documents. Associate Planner
  continued her presentation summarizing the staff report.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve PA-
  210244 subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked about the timeframe to receive the records from the County.
  Associate Planner Thom stated that the records request was submitted today and may take a few
  weeks due to closure of County offices due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Associate Planner Thom stated that
  the survey identifies a boundary and does not discuss an easement. COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG
  commented that it will need to be determined whether there was an easement when the lot was
  split.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR commented that he has a comparable situation with one of his
  properties and it was not able to be determined if there was an easement. He would not like to see
  the Planning Commission involved in a situation that would delay the project.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that Condition of Approval No. 3, references a deferral for the
  approval of the location of the swimming pool and equipment that could potentially encroach within
  the easement and subjects it to later approval to the satisfaction of the City Attorney once staff has
  received recorded documents and is able to verify whether it is a recorded easement.

  In response to a question by CHAIR EDLER, Planning Manager Naughton stated that if recorded
  documents were found that showed that conditions of approval in the 1966 lot split were
  effectuated, then the applicants would be asked to relocate the pool and equipment.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if it would be best to wait for the easement issue to be addressed,
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the approval would be for the home itself and Condition
  of Approval No. 3 would defer the approval of the pool and equipment which would relieve any
  discrepancy with the easement. Associate Planner Thom added that it would include the pool, pool
  equipment, and future horse keeping area.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed her concern with the glass front of the home and its
  compatibility with other homes in the neighborhood.

  CHAIR EDLER opened the public comment period.

  Joseph Dangaran, Applicant and Architect stated that his wife Sabna grew up in the Peninsula and
  attended Chadwick School; two of her siblings attended Peninsula High School. They currently
  reside in Culver City and he is excited to bring his family to Rolling Hills Estates. Mr. Dangaran
  stated that the allure of this property is that it is almost one acre, and they can design a single-story
  home that, he believes, is much less impactful on the neighborhood. This home is being proposed
  at a height of fourteen feet to the top of the ridge, where they are allowed two stories at twenty-
  seven feet. Mr. Dangaran stated that he is aware of how construction activity could impact the
  neighborhood and has submitted a construction parking plan to the City for workers, who will be
  able to park on their property during construction. They have also reached out to adjacent
  neighbors informing them of this project. Mr. Dangaran provided a brief presentation with the
  architectural inspiration for the design of the home, which he stated, “leaned heavily on Cliff May.”
  Mr. Dangaran added that there are no easements recorded for this property and the title report is
  clear from prior owners.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he is familiar with Cliff May homes and stated that this
  building fits in well with this style. He added that this is not the typical Ranch style that is seen in
  the city, but could be referred to as a Modern Ranch style and would like to see more of these
  homes in the city. COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he is in favor of this project.

  CHAIR EDLER agreed and applauded the applicant on a high-quality job and presentation. He
  also commented that more applicants should consider neighbor’s concerns during the construction
  process as this applicant has done with providing on-site parking for workers. CHAIR EDLER
  stated that this will be a good addition to the neighborhood and to the city.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR agreed and commended the applicant on implementing a beautiful
  plan that will enhance that corner and stated that he is favor of this project.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, AUGUST 2, 2021
  2
   COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210244 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

  AYES: EDLER, MEDAWAR, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES: CARMAN
  ABSENT: SCOTT
  ABSTAIN: SCHACTHER

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. PA-210244, A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-
  210245) to demolish the existing single-story home to construct a new single-story residence. An
  appeal of the Planning Commission decision may be made by any aggrieved party or the City
  Council in its own motion within 20 days after the Planning Commission renders its decision.

  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210125; ADDRESS: 2665 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: OLYMPIA PILAFIDIS, AIA,
  GREER & ASSOCIATES, AIA ARCHITECTS; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination (NC-210126) for proposed one- and two-story additions to an existing one-
  story single-family residence. The request includes expansion of an existing Accessory
  Dwelling Unit (ADU) and new garage for the ADU. A Minor Deviation (MD-210127) is
  required for an encroachment into a required front yard of a developed residential lot, which
  does not project closer to the front property line that the forwardmost building line.

  Planning Manager Naughton presented Planning Application No. PA-210125. This 35,128 sq ft
  property is zoned RA-20 and has a general plan land use designation of low density residential
  and is in the horse overlay zone. The existing property was developed in 1950 with a 1,200 sq ft
  one-story single-family residence, a 590 sq ft accessory dwelling unit (ADU), and detached garage.
  The proposed project is for 1,800 sq ft of new living area on the main floor, 1,600 sq ft on the
  second floor, demolish the detached garage and attach a 512 sq ft garage to the main house. The
  applicants are proposing to expand the existing ADU to approximately 976 sq ft with an attached
  336 sq ft garage. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the ADU and respective garage are
  ministerially allowed under Section 17.56 and the use has not been brought for discretionary
  review, however, it has been included for the overall massing of the development. Planning
  Manager Naughton continued the presentation with details of the overall design of the proposed
  project.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
  Planning Applicant No. PA-210125 subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the size of the ADU. Planning Manager Naughton stated
  that the garage is not included as part of the livable area, however, the ADU and garage are
  included as part of the overall lot coverage.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the pool pavilion. Planning Manager Naughton stated
  that the pool pavilion and outdoor kitchen is also included in the overall lot coverage.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the .75 multiplier. Planning Manager Naughton stated
  that the Municipal Code counts hardscape and structures, such as swimming pools, at a rate of
  .75 whereas roofed structures and building footprint are counted at a rate of 1.0.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the turf block. Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  turf block is counted at a rate of .50 and if in the future it was converted to hardscape, that it would
  become an enforcement issue.

  CHAIR EDLER opened the public comment period.

  Olympia Pilafidis, Architect with Greer & Associates Architects, provided a presentation of the
  proposed project including history on the existing home and minor improvements done to the home
  since it was originally built in 1949. Ms. Pilafidis stated that the owner, Mr. Frangos, had several
  ideas for developing this lot and ultimately decided to build one large home where he and his
  daughter, who is soon to be married, could live comfortably close to each other. Ms. Pilafidis
  continued with a presentation with details of the design.

  Stephanie Frangos, Daughter of Property Owner, read a statement from her father, Steve Frangos,
  Property Owner. Ms. Frangos stated that she is in full support of her father’s plans to build this
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, AUGUST 2, 2021
  3
   home and stated that she and her fiancé plan to get married next year and their goal is to be closer
  to her parents. This will allow for her parents to be close to their future grandchildren. In return, it
  will allow her to be close to them and provide any assistance they may need in the future. Ms.
  Frangos emphasized that she is their only child, and this project is important to her. She added
  that this property always had great potential and a lot of space to build. She attended Palos Verdes
  High School and always envisioned this house to get bigger and allow their families to live
  comfortably and cheerfully.

  CHAIR EDLER closed the public comment period.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that Ms. Pilafidis has done a nice job with this project and the
  stepping of the roof line and stated that he is in favor of this project.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he likes the plan and consideration of the setbacks and
  is in favor of the project.

  COMMISSIONER YOO stated that the plan build out is consistent with what the Planning
  Commission has requested from other homeowners and can support this project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she likes the architectural style and the architect’s effort to
  minimize the appearance from Palos Verdes Drive North, and that it is a good use of space and
  she is happy to see this project come before the Planning Commission.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG made a motion, seconded by CHAIR EDLER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210125 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

  AYES: EDLER, CARMAN, MEDAWAR, SCHACTHER, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES:
  ABSENT: SCOTT
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. PA-210125, A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-
  210126) for proposed one- and two-story additions to an existing one-story single-family residence.
  A Minor Deviation (MD-210127) is required for an encroachment into a required front yard of a
  developed residential lot, which does not project closer to the front property line that the
  forwardmost building line. An appeal of the Planning Commission decision may be made by any
  aggrieved party or the City Council in its own motion within 20 days after the Planning Commission
  renders its decision.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210231; ADDRESS: 11 MONTECILLO DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: PETER SMITH, ON BEHALF OF THE
  JACK KRAMER CLUB; A request to approve a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-210232) to
  amend CUP-102-87, revising the parking requirement methodology to be consistent with
  current standards. There are no proposed expansions to existing facilities or programming
  schedules.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that no discussion be conducted at this
  time and that this item be continued to the September 7th Planning Commission meeting to allow
  the applicant sufficient time to meet with the Montecillo HOA.

  The applicants were trying to secure a meeting with the Montecillo HOA and that meeting occurred
  this past Friday. Staff felt that it would be most beneficial to allow time for any additional input to be
  provided and continue this item to the September meeting, when staff has had an opportunity to
  incorporate any comments that may be received from the HOA into the proposed conditions for the
  project. She added that this project will be re-published and re-noticed.

  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210227; ADDRESS: 2 SILVER SADDLE LANE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: MR. AND MRS. KOSUKE AND
  CHIEKO TOKUNAGA; A Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210228) to legalize
  unpermitted construction and site work, including an attached covered porch and retaining
  walls within the front yard setback. A Minor Deviation (MD-210229) is required to decrease
  the front yard area by less than 10%. A Variance (V-210230) is required to build beyond the
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, AUGUST 2, 2021
  4
   forwardmost building line.

  Associate Planner Thom presented Planning Application No. PA-210227, legalization of
  unpermitted construction and site work. The work involves a partially-built attached covered porch,
  built within the front yard setback along the Palos Verdes Lane side of the property. In addition,
  retaining walls around the property were revised to bring them down to comply with the zoning code.
  A comment opposing the project was received today. Associate Planner Thom stated that the
  applicant still needs to make changes as noted on the plan, to be more neighborhood compatible.
  A Minor Deviation to decrease the front yard area by less than 10% and a Variance to build beyond
  the forwardmost building line is requested, given that the property was developed with a
  substandard rear yard setback, 35 ft is the minimum and this property is at approximately 9 ft, which
  is a hardship. In addition, there is little usable backyard on this property. Associate Planner Thom
  continued with the presentation describing the property and detail and providing images of the
  existing and proposed design of the home.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open the
  public hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt
  Resolution No. PA-210227 approving the project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN requested clarification on what is being described as a patio. Associate
  Thom stated that there will be modifications to what currently exists on the property; the construction
  as it stands does not depict what is shown on the plans.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG commented that there will likely be extensive investigate work that will
  be necessary by LA County Building and Safety for the unpermitted footings that already exist on
  this property, but they would need to get through this process first. Associate Planning Thom
  confirmed.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked when the unpermitted construction begin. Associate Planner Thom
  stated that a violation notice was sent by the City’s Code Compliance Officer to the property owner
  in November of 2020.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the existing wall will be demolished. Associate Planner
  Thom stated that it may come down, but what exists is not exactly what is reflected on the plans. It
  is her understanding there will need to be significant demolition of what currently exists.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired why this plan has been brought before the Planning
  Commission since the plans seem to be incomplete.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about the material being used for the patio. Associate Planner
  stated that it may be concrete material.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there is a requirement to silhouette the new roof line for the patio.
  Associate Planner Thom stated that for one story homes, there is some discretion for staff when
  there is view blockage, but this is determined by staff.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that there are other areas that could have been added to this
  house and he is not in favor of this project.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he has issues with this project going up and footings being
  poured without permits. He would like to see clear plans of what the front façade will look like. If this
  project comes back with the same type of slanted roof and add-on, he could not approve the project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed her concern with the current condition and what the intent
  is with the existing unpermitted work. COMMISSIONER CARMAN referred to one of the conditions
  of the resolution for this project and is concerned that if all of the work complies with building code,
  this solution would not be acceptable visually due to its prominent location. COMMISSIONER

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, AUGUST 2, 2021
  5
   CARMAN stated that she would like to see a clean slate without the exception of the current
  modifications that have been made.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked for clarification on the procedure on code enforcement issues.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that typically the applicant will need to contact the Planning
  Department and if the unpermitted work could be legalized by simply getting building permits, this
  is the preferred course of action. If entitlements need to be applied for, such as with this case, then
  the applicant would need to submit plans for Planning Commission review.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the applicant has been cooperative with respect to the enforcement
  respect. Planning Manager Naughton stated that they have, however, because of the applicant’s
  level of knowledge with building, it was difficult to get plans for this project in a timely manner.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that this case should be continued to a date uncertain and
  directed staff to reach out to the applicant with the Planning Commission’s input on the plans. He
  suggested a nice open patio, however, the roof design is not good. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that continuing this application will be very beneficial to the applicant. Staff will relay all of the
  concerns brought up by the Planning Commission, ask for different design and ideas, more complete
  plans including a demolition plan, before resetting a hearing date.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG made a motion, seconded by CHAIR EDLER to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210227 TO A DATE UNCERTAIN TO
  PROVIDE SUFFICIENT TIME FOR STAFF TO PROVIDE FEEDBACK AND WORK WITH
  THE APPLICANT.

  AYES: EDLER, CARMAN, MEDAWAR, SCHACTHER, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES:
  ABSENT: SCOTT
  ABSTAIN:

  9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS
